slot.brief: Radioactive decay: given fraction of a sample remaining after a given time, determine the half-life; or given half-life determine number of half-lives in a stated activity-drop period.

stem: A radioactive sample has $\dfrac{1}{8}$ of its original nuclei remaining after $18$ hours. What is its half-life?

verdicts.working: Since 1/8 = (1/2)^3, 18 hours is 3 half-lives. Thus the half-life is 18/3 = 6 h.

working:
$\dfrac{N}{N_0}=\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^n=\dfrac{1}{8}=\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^3$
$n=3$; $T_{1/2}=\dfrac{18}{3}=6$ h

Independent check: Since 1/8 = (1/2)^3, 18 hours is 3 half-lives. Thus the half-life is 18/3 = 6 h.
solution: The remaining fraction after $n$ half-lives is $\left(\frac12\right)^n$. Since $\frac18=\left(\frac12\right)^3$, 18 hours is 3 half-lives. $$T_{1/2}=\frac{18}{3}=6\text{ h}$$
